subject.title: [Bug P2] scheduleReconnect() has no max retry limit — infinite reconnect loop

question: Should GatewayClient keep unlimited reconnects by default and expose an opt-in cap only for short-lived callers, or should OpenClaw change the default reconnect policy globally?
rationale: The source-level unbounded scheduler is clear, but node-host currently relies on long-lived recovery, so the permanent retry contract is a compatibility and product decision rather than a purely mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Opt-in bounded reconnect
options.body: Keep node-host unlimited by default, add the cap in `packages/gateway-client`, and wire only maintainer-approved short-lived clients to the bounded policy.

options.title: Global retry cap
options.body: Make every GatewayClient stop after a fixed number of attempts, accepting the risk that long-lived node hosts no longer recover automatically after extended outages.

options.title: Keep current behavior
options.body: Treat unlimited reconnect as intentional recovery behavior and close the issue only if maintainers accept and document the resource-risk tradeoff.

recommendation.title: Opt-in bounded reconnect
recommendation.body: Keep node-host unlimited by default, add the cap in `packages/gateway-client`, and wire only maintainer-approved short-lived clients to the bounded policy.

likelyOwner.reason: The original Gateway WebSocket control-plane behavior traces to this owner path, and the decision is about the long-term gateway retry contract.
